title: Multiplication machine halting
statement: Let $x,a,b,c$ be finite bit strings with $x=\langle a,\langle b,c\rangle\rangle$, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of the machine’s $13$ registers. Suppose every register value is at most $4(|x|+1)$, register $1$ contains $|x|$, registers $2$ and $3$ contain $2|a|+2$ and $2|a|+2+2|b|+2$, respectively, and registers $4,5,6,7,11,12$ are all zero. Starting in the copy stage with these register values and no answer recorded, the multiplication machine halts with answer true exactly when $x$ belongs to the language of encoded multiplication instances.
hypotheses_covered: Every register value is at most $4(|x|+1)$
